newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Jan 4 Initial Claims from 361,000 and Dec 28 from 374,000; Jan 4 Four-Week Average from 357,250 and Dec 28 from 354,500; Dec 28 Continued Claims from 2,509,000 and Dec 21 from 2,554,000.
Wall Street economists had forcast initial jobless claims of 355,000 in the January 11 week.
The department said 17 states and one territory reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended January 4, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Wisconsin, with 12,094; Michigan, with 10,137; Kentucky, with 8,746; Illinois, with 8,713; Massachusetts, with 7,676; and Iowa, with 7,108.
Wisconsin reported fewer layoffs in manufacturing, and the construction, trade and service industries while Michigan reported fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state.

Kentucky had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment, rubber and primary metals industries and Illinois had fewer layoffs in the construction and service industries and in manufacturing. Massachusetts and Iowa provided no explanation.
Labor said 11 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the January 4 week.
Among the largest were North Carolina, with 27,879; New York, with 19,998; South Carolina, with 12,355; Alabama, with 10,049; and California, with 6,175.

North Carolina reported layoffs in the construction, service, textile, apparel, furniture, lumber, rubber and glass industries and manufucturing. New York had layoffs in the construction and service industries, as well as holiday shutdowns in various industries.

South Carolina reported layoffs in the textile industry while Alabama said there were layoffs in the textile, apparel and lumber industries and in manufacturing. California had layoffs in the construction, trade, service and transportation industries. It also reported layoffs in agriculture, as well as holiday shutdowns in various industries.
